taskTrace.description: Phase 08.02: define and implement a dedicated operator-only administrator-bootstrap CLI for local development, deployed development, and production. Resolve one existing user by an explicitly supplied normalized email using the configured encrypted-email lookup path, with an optional UUID selector only as an advanced alternative; require an existing verified Login Method and real credential; permit only first-administrator creation; make same-target replay a no-op and refuse promotion when another administrator exists; serialize concurrent attempts; atomically persist the role change and a truthful operator-origin audit record; require explicit environment and production confirmation; emit no credential, email, database URL, encryption detail, or other PII; remove the unusable seeded administrator; and document mandatory sign-out/sign-in for fresh role and verification claims. Do not add a public role-promotion endpoint or mark email verified during bootstrap.
taskTrace.verificationCriteria: Design and operator documentation define authorization, environment, audit-actor, and reauthentication semantics. Unit and isolated PostgreSQL integration tests cover normalized/case-insensitive email resolution, exact target selection, initial bootstrap, target-not-found and unverified-user rejection, unauthorized or incorrectly targeted environment denial, explicit production confirmation, concurrent attempts producing one administrator and one audit effect, same-target idempotent replay, refusal when a different administrator exists, and rollback when audit persistence fails. CLI tests prove interactive email input can avoid shell history, UUID selection remains optional, output contains only safe identifiers/result/audit metadata, and captured stdout/stderr contain no supplied email, credentials, database URL, key material, hashes, salts, tokens, or cookies. Seed tests prove no unusable administrator account is created, authentication tests prove existing sessions retain old claims until reauthentication, the installed `golang-security` review passes, and focused tests pass under `go test -race`.

taskTrace.component: Phase 08.02 JSON Global Catalog Import Operator
taskTrace.description: Phase 08.02: add `scripts/import-global-catalog.py` as an explicit operator tool for importing at most 500 global food items per run through the existing authenticated `POST /api/v1/admin/items` route. Accept a versioned `mealswapp.global-catalog.v1` JSON document with one stable operator-supplied `Idempotency-Key` per item, metric nutritional/serving/density fields, canonical micronutrient keys, canonical allergen keys, portable classification names by default, and optional classification UUIDs as an advanced alternative. Extend the manual administration request and persistence contract so validated active `allergenKeys` are atomically stored with each global item. Validate the complete document and resolve active classifications and allergens before the first mutation; provide authenticated `--dry-run`, interactive password entry, in-memory cookies, fresh CSRF acquisition, bounded 2.1-second request pacing, bounded `Retry-After` handling, same-key retry for ambiguous transport/5xx outcomes, deterministic resumable reruns, sanitized per-item reporting, and nonzero exit status on partial failure. Do not add a public bulk-import endpoint, write directly to PostgreSQL, accept imperial persistence fields, derive idempotency keys from item positions, or store/print credentials, cookies, CSRF tokens, emails, request bodies, or other PII.
taskTrace.verificationCriteria: Unit tests cover version/schema rejection, duplicate JSON keys, duplicate/invalid idempotency keys, malformed items, metric solid/liquid and density rules, unknown or ambiguous classification names, unknown micronutrients or allergens, classification-name and optional UUID resolution, canonical allergen resolution, the 500-item limit, zero-mutation dry-run, stable report ordering, safe key fingerprints, interrupted-run rerun, and credential/PII-safe stdout, stderr, and report files. HTTP/fake-server tests prove login uses an interactive non-argument password, cookies remain in memory, CSRF is refreshed after login, one create request is sent per valid item, 30-mutations-per-minute pacing is not exceeded, valid bounded `Retry-After` is honored, network/5xx ambiguity retries with the identical key and body, exact replay succeeds without duplication, changed-body key reuse fails, 400/409 item failures are permanent, 401/403 abort the run, and partial failure exits nonzero. Isolated PostgreSQL/Redis integration tests prove normal domain validation, atomic classification/allergen persistence, one ownerless item/audit/cache invalidation per successful create, no mutation during failed preflight, resumable replay without duplicates, and decodable contract-conforming manual-item, classification, and allergen responses; the known manual-item success-envelope and classification-UUID defects must be resolved before this task can pass. Operator documentation defines the moderate-volume threshold and directs larger datasets to a separately designed offline ingestion path; OpenAPI/generated contracts, focused Python tests, backend integration tests, `golang-security` review, traceability validation, and `git diff --check` pass.

taskTrace.description: Phase 08.02: add a restricted authenticated `GET /api/v1/admin/catalog-export` read API and `scripts/export-global-catalog.py` operator client for exporting the complete ownerless global catalog without conflating it with user Account Export. Use the authoritative versioned `mealswapp.global-catalog.v1` JSON representation shared with Task 277, active items by default, explicit `--include-deleted`, JSON and human-inspection CSV formats, optional pretty JSON, deterministic item/classification/allergen/property ordering and numeric encoding, stable export idempotency keys derived from item UUIDs, and no volatile generated timestamp. Include IDs, names, physical state, preparation time, metric serving/unit/density fields and provenance, macros, micronutrients, image URL/alt metadata, source provider/external ID metadata, timestamps, Food Category and Culinary Role relationships, canonical allergens, and deletion state. Export curated-source identity as informational metadata but document that import through the manual-item route does not recreate `curated_imports` records. Reuse the importer’s interactive credential and in-memory session helper; stream a read-only consistent PostgreSQL snapshot to a same-directory temporary file, flush and fsync it, atomically replace the destination only after success, preserve any prior destination on failure, emit only safe path/count/request metadata, and return nonzero on every partial or complete failure.
taskTrace.verificationCriteria: OpenAPI and authorization tests prove the export route is administration-only, anonymous and ordinary users receive 401/403, `includeDeleted` defaults false, unsupported parameters/formats fail safely, the endpoint cannot expose private custom items or Account Export PII, and logs contain no credentials, cookies, tokens, emails, item names, or payloads. Repository/service/API tests use a read-only transaction and bounded streaming to verify a single consistent snapshot, stable UUID ordering, sorted relationships and micronutrient/allergen keys, exact metric values, Unicode, null optional fields, solids, liquids, source/image metadata, active/deleted selection, empty and large catalogs, deterministic byte-identical reruns for unchanged state, and safe cancellation/error propagation. Python tests cover `--output`, `--format`, `--pretty`, `--include-deleted`, interactive non-argument passwords, JSON/CSV parsing, summary counts, same-directory temporary files, fsync plus atomic replacement, interrupted writes, preservation of an existing destination, nonzero failures, and credential/PII-safe stdout and stderr. Round-trip tests export then re-import the supported manual-item fields, classifications, micronutrients, density provenance, images, and allergens without duplication while proving curated-import metadata is reported but not falsely recreated; OpenAPI lint/generated drift, focused backend/Python tests, `go test -race`, `golang-security` review, traceability validation, and `git diff --check` pass.

taskTrace.component: Phase 08.02 Isolated Real-Stack Administration E2E Harness
taskTrace.description: Phase 08.02: replace shared-development-state execution in `scripts/verify-task-261-ui.sh` and `frontend/tests/task261-real-admin-flow.spec.ts` with a reusable `scripts/run-real-stack-e2e.py` harness that owns one disposable PostgreSQL database, Redis instance, API process, frontend process, and Playwright run. Generate a strict `mealswapp_e2e_<opaque-run-id>_test` database name and matching ownership comment, apply migrations without development seeds, start a run-labeled disposable Redis container, allocate independent API/frontend ports with a configurable Vite proxy target, bootstrap the explicitly registered fixture administrator through Task 276 instead of direct SQL, retain created IDs for assertions, export sanitized logs/traces/screenshots before teardown, and destroy only the run-owned environment after success, assertion failure, timeout, cancellation, or handled signals. Add an explicit age-bounded `--cleanup-stale` recovery mode for killed runs. Never target `mealswapp`, production, a non-loopback database, an unmarked or non-`_test` database, a Redis instance not owned by the run, name-prefix fixture rows, broad schema/table truncation, or Redis `FLUSHALL`.
taskTrace.verificationCriteria: Harness unit tests mock process, PostgreSQL, Docker, port, signal, and filesystem boundaries and prove unsafe database/environment/host names are rejected before connection; database deletion requires both the exact generated-name pattern and matching ownership comment; Redis cleanup requires the exact run label; stale cleanup requires the documented minimum age; and diagnostics contain run IDs/request IDs but no credentials, cookies, CSRF tokens, emails, names, bodies, or database URLs. Isolated integration tests prove migrations and API/Redis readiness use only run-owned targets, Vite proxies to the allocated API port, Task 261 performs no direct SQL or `node:child_process` promotion, and artifacts survive environment teardown. The real browser suite passes twice sequentially and in concurrent independent runs; injected assertion failure, API timeout, `INT`/`TERM`/`HUP`, and a simulated killed process leave the development database/catalog and unrelated Redis keys byte-for-byte/logically unchanged, remove all ordinarily owned resources, and leave only the intentional stale fixture that `--cleanup-stale` removes idempotently after its age guard.
